subject: Ownership boundaries & feedback license — proposed compromise
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Chen <rachel.chen@acme-corp.com>, Daniel Park <d.park@lexbridgelaw.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Marked MSA + order form redlines (training / output concerns)

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the order form. Our legal team reviewed the MSA and we attached markups focusing on two points that are blockers for procurement: who owns "output" and whether Redwood can use customer data/outputs for model training or continuous improvement. Our asks:

- Customer retains exclusive title to customer-provided content and outputs (they want explicit "title" language).
- No use of customer data or outputs for model retraining or improving models without express opt-in (they want a perpetual, global restriction).

We understand product-level telemetry/metrics are necessary, but they want a carveout that excludes anything considered "Customer Confidential Data" or derived outputs.

Attached: ACME_MSA_redlines_20270919.docx (docx) and OrderForm_ACME_v3.pdf (pdf).

Can your legal team propose countertext? We're happy to set up a short call with Daniel (our counsel) if that helps.

—Sofia
Customer Procurement, Acme Corp

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com, dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Marked MSA + order form redlines (training / output concerns)

Team — forwarding Acme's redlines. Key commercial ask: they want explicit title to outputs + a blanket prohibition on using outputs/data for model training without opt-in. Procurement is stalled unless we land a middle ground.

Notes / constraints from product:
- We cannot promise zero usage of telemetry; need aggregated telemetry for system reliability.
- For continuous improvement we sometimes use de-identified snippets to tune serving models; legal needs to limit scope (no customer PII, no verbatim outputs).

Proposed next steps:
1) Draft a short "feedback license" snippet that gives Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use non-confidential, aggregated telemetry and feedback for service quality and safety improvements, with an explicit exclusion for Customer Confidential Data and outputs that contain PII or proprietary content.
2) Offer Acme an opt-out checkbox on Order Form (paid tier) for model training — but call this a paid feature (enterprise privacy package).
3) If Acme insists on title, propose an attribution-style clause instead of "title transfer" for outputs generated solely by the customer prompts (i.e., customer has rights to use outputs, Redwood retains rights to generalize learnings).

Dylan, can you propose redline language for the feedback/license snippet? Laura/Evelyn — any commercial/discount concessions to reframe as a paid privacy add-on?

Marcus
VP, Account — Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Marked MSA + order form redlines (training / output concerns)

Marcus / team — draft redline below (keeps it tight, purpose-limited):

"Feedback & Service Improvement License (proposed):
Customer grants Redwood a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use anonymized, aggregated usage data and feedback ("Telemetry") solely to operate, maintain, and improve Redwood's services (including model safety and quality). Telemetry expressly excludes Customer Confidential Data, Customer Personal Data, and any Outputs as defined below. "Outputs" means content generated by Redwood in response to Customer prompts. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may opt-in via Order Form to allow Redwood to use de-identified Outputs for model training and research under mutually agreed terms.
"

Rationale:
- Keeps default position protective of customer outputs.
- Provides a commercial path (opt-in) for training that we can upsell.
- Avoids language that looks like assignment of title.

I can turn that into a tracked-change doc if you want. Laura — if we make opt-in a paid add-on, what would be a reasonable uplift (percent) to propose?

—Dylan
Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acme-corp.com>, Rachel Chen <rachel.chen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <d.park@lexbridgelaw.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com, dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Marked MSA + order form redlines (training / output concerns)

Sofia / Rachel — thanks for the redlines and the clarity on Acme's position. We've reviewed with our legal and product teams and propose the below compromise to move procurement forward:

1) No assignment of title: Redwood will not claim title to Customer Outputs. Customer retains rights to use Outputs as produced under the Agreement.

2) Default license: Customer grants Redwood a limited, perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use anonymized, aggregated Telemetry for service operation, reliability, and safety improvements. Telemetry explicitly excludes Customer Confidential Data, Customer Personal Data, and verbatim Outputs that contain proprietary content.

3) Opt-in training: If Acme wants Redwood to use Outputs for model training or to include Outputs in a corpus for model improvement, Acme can opt in via the Order Form. Opt-in is a paid enterprise feature; we will document the scope (types of de-identification, retention, and access controls) and sign a minimal SOW if required.

4) Audit & controls: We will include standard technical controls (data minimization, de-identification, and audit logs) and provide high-level attestation. For customers with regulatory needs we can extend logging retention and KMS controls under the Private deployment offering.

Next steps:
- Laura/Evelyn: confirm commercial uplift and language for Order Form opt-in.
- Sofia/Daniel: please confirm if Acme would accept opt-in as a paid feature or whether procurement requires a no-training guarantee (in which case we can discuss concession credits).
- Suggest a 30-minute call tomorrow to close.

Thanks — happy to join a brief call with Daniel to walk through the specifics.

Marcus Lin
VP, Accounts | Redwood Inference
